purpose: Ibuprofen is used to relieve pain, reduce fever, and lower inflammation. It works well for headaches, muscle aches, toothaches, menstrual cramps, and minor arthritis pain. It can also bring down a fever when you or your child is feeling sick.
how_it_works: Your body makes certain chemicals called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling, and fever. Ibuprofen blocks the enzymes that produce these chemicals, so you feel less pain and inflammation. Think of it like turning down the volume on your body's pain and swelling signals.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include upset stomach, nausea, heartburn, and indigestion. Some people may also notice mild headache or dizziness. Taking it with food or milk usually helps reduce stomach discomfort.
warnings: Do not take ibuprofen if you have a history of stomach ulcers, kidney problems, or heart disease without first talking to your doctor. Avoid it if you are pregnant, especially in the last 3 months. Do not use it with alcohol, as this increases the risk of stomach bleeding. Always use the lowest dose that works for the shortest time needed.
typical_dosing: For adults and teens over 12, the usual dose is 200 to 400 mg taken every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Do not take more than 1200 mg in 24 hours unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Always take it with food or a full glass of water to protect your stomach.
